glossary.definition: The lab's story: a support engineer holds the Minimum Access profile and nothing else, so Salesforce Cases is denied. A P1 lands, the engineer asks for the Case Read Access permission set with a note and an end time, Privilege grants it, and Cases lists the P1. Ending the access deletes the policy; Cases is denied again and a receipt remains. The Cases view is the lab's mock; "The old way" panel is narrative, not a Privilege claim.

Privilege signs in to Salesforce as one integration user with a signed JWT: no password, no consent screen. It works only when the External Client App has JWT Bearer Flow with Privilege's certificate and the scopes api and refresh_token, offline_access; Permitted Users is "Admin approved users are pre-authorized"; and a permission set is linked to the app and assigned to the signing-in user.

The generic error ("user hasn't approved this consumer") Salesforce gave when pre-authorization, the permission set link or the assignment was missing, or when a change had not propagated (up to 10 minutes).

Privilege links a Salesforce user to a Privilege user only when the emails are identical; Federation ID did not override it, and an email on two Privilege records is refused ("its email matches 2 Privilege users").
The Developer org had 4 Salesforce user seats, and a Salesforce username is unique across all orgs ("Duplicate username").
A grant is refused for a set that needs a permission set license, whose user license differs from the user's, or that the user already holds ("Already has this permission set").

There is no Revoke button: deleting the policy shows "Revoke pending, access still live" on the policy. In the guide the removal is queued and a refresh shows it: the assignment is gone in Salesforce and the policy count drops to 0.
Access Receipts shows user, set, end date and status Granted, and later the guide's Expired / Revoked counter; the reconciliation line reads 1 confirmed while Salesforce holds the assignment.

sources.use: A file in this lab's own repository (not a web page): every behaviour the mock models, from one real setup done once.

cards.label: Scenario 1: Support P1: no access, access for the job, no access again
cards.description: Omar Reyes is a support engineer with the Minimum Access profile and no access to Cases. A P1 lands: Omar Reyes asks for Case Read Access with a note and an end time, Privilege grants it, and Cases lists the P1. Ending the access deletes the policy: first "Revoke pending, access still live", then the assignment is gone and Cases is denied again. The receipt keeps the record.

cards.label: Scenario 2: Connect, link, grant, revoke
cards.description: The whole cycle once, with nothing going wrong: connect the org, link Omar Reyes, grant Case Read Access for a window, see it in Salesforce, delete the policy and see it gone.

cards.label: Scenario 3: Sign-in fails: invalid_client_id
cards.description: The Consumer Key was copied wrongly. Salesforce answers invalid_client_id; copy it again.

cards.label: Scenario 4: Sign-in fails: not propagated yet
cards.description: Everything is right, but the app was only just created. invalid_grant, "user hasn't approved this consumer", until the lab clock has moved forward a few minutes.

cards.label: Scenario 5: Sign-in fails: not pre-authorized
cards.description: Permitted Users was left at "All users can self-authorize", which does not work for JWT. invalid_grant.

cards.label: Scenario 6: Sign-in fails: refresh_token scope missing
cards.description: Without refresh_token, offline_access Salesforce rejects the flow.

cards.label: Scenario 7: Sign-in fails: certificate does not match the key
cards.description: The wizard was refreshed (a new key), so the certificate uploaded to the app no longer matches. Upload the new .crt.

cards.label: Scenario 8: Sign-in fails: permission set not linked, then not assigned
cards.description: Both look the same from outside: invalid_grant. The permission set must be linked to the app and assigned to the signing-in user.

cards.label: Scenario 9: Link refused: its email matches 2 Privilege users
cards.description: Two Privilege records share an email, so neither links. Federation ID does not help; pick a user whose email is unique.

cards.label: Scenario 10: Link pitfalls: Federation ID, duplicate username, no seats
cards.description: A Federation ID does not rescue a mismatched email, a Salesforce username is unique across all orgs, and the observed org had 4 seats.

cards.label: Scenario 11: Grant refused: license rules and "Already has"
cards.description: Some permission sets need a permission set license, some belong to a different user license, and one the user already holds cannot be granted twice.

cards.label: Scenario 12: Revoke by deleting the policy
cards.description: There is no Revoke button: delete the policy. First "Revoke pending, access still live", then the assignment is gone in Salesforce.

cards.label: Support P1: the story
cards.description: Three panels together: the engineer's Salesforce view, Privilege, and "The old way". Request access (the engineer's note and end time are the lab's own step), work the P1, End access, Refresh receipts; Cases goes from denied, to three cases, to denied again, and the receipt shows Granted then Expired / Revoked.

cards.label: Scenarios: the scripted runs
cards.description: Twelve scripted scenarios run step by step by the lab's own engine, each step with its raw request and response.

cards.label: Connect: the wizard rehearsal
cards.description: Org URL, key and certificate, the External Client App, then the sign-in check: every failure comes back with its cause and the exact fix.

cards.label: Link: Add Users and Sync
cards.description: Add a Privilege user and Sync: identical email only, the shared-email refusal, the four licence seats and the duplicate-username refusal.

cards.label: Grant and revoke
cards.description: Grant a permission set with a duration, watch the receipt and the reconciliation, then delete the policy: the policy reads Revoke pending, access still live, and Refresh receipts shows it gone.

cards.label: Diagrams
cards.description: Two diagrams loaded by name from the server: connect and link, and grant and revoke. Movable boxes, Simulate, speed, Reset.

cards.label: Real: one read of your own org (owner only)
cards.description: Run scripts/setup-real.sh once, switch to Real, type the org host to confirm, and read one org's permission sets and users. Read-only, one origin, the key and the token are never shown.

cards.label: Presenter mode and the talk track
cards.description: Press P for presenter mode (the simulation banner stays) and open the talk track: the three beats of the Support P1 story, then one part per page.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.

diagrams.label: Connect an org and link a user
